questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are related to ecosystem?

(i) It consists of biotic components comprising living organisms.

(ii) All green plants and certain bacteria are producers.

(iii) Decomposers break-down complex organic into simple organic substance.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3) Only (i) and (ii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An ecosystem comprises both biotic (living organisms) and abiotic (non-living elements) components.
 
• Green plants and certain bacteria are producers because they can manufacture their own food through photosynthesis or chemosynthesis.
 
• Decomposers, such as fungi and bacteria, break down dead organic matter into simpler inorganic substances, recycling nutrients back into the ecosystem.
 
• Statements (i) and (ii) are correct. Statement (iii) is incorrect because decomposers break down complex organic substances into simple inorganic substances, not organic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ecosystem:**

 
 
• An ecosystem is a community of living organisms (plants, animals, and microbes) interacting with their physical environment (air, water, soil).
 
• It involves both biotic and abiotic components that interact as a system.
 
• Energy flows through an ecosystem in one direction—usually from the sun, through photosynthetic organisms (producers), to herbivores (consumers), and finally to decomposers.
 
 
 
• **Producers:**
 
 
• Producers, or autotrophs, are organisms that produce their own food through photosynthesis (using sunlight) or chemosynthesis (using chemical energy).
 
• Examples include green plants, algae, and certain bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Consumers:**
 
 
• Consumers, or heterotrophs, are organisms that cannot produce their own food and depend on other organisms for nutrition.
 
• They are categorized into primary consumers (herbivores), secondary consumers (carnivores that eat herbivores), and tertiary consumers (carnivores that eat other carnivores).
 
 
 
• **Decomposers:**
 
 
• Decomposers are organisms that break down dead or decaying organisms, and in doing so, carry out the natural process of decomposition.
 
• They play a critical role in nutrient cycling by converting organic materials back into inorganic substances, which can be used by producers.
 
• Examples include fungi, bacteria, and certain insects.

questions.question: Which biotic component of an ecosystem is present in the greatest number?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Producers**__.

**Note:** As per the official answer key, the correct answer is** Tertiary Consumers **but in actual the correct answer would be **Producers** because producers form the base of the ecological pyramid. As they are the primary source of energy for all other organisms in the ecosystem, producers are the most abundant biotic component.

**Source: ** https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lebo114.pdf

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Producers** are the organisms in an ecosystem that produce energy-rich compounds like glucose through photosynthesis.
 
• They form the base of the food chain and are critical for energy flow in an ecosystem.
 
• Examples of producers include **plants, algae, and cyanobacteria**.
 
• Producers convert sunlight into chemical energy, which is utilized by all other biotic components.
 
• Their large numbers are essential for supporting the energy needs of the entire ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Primary Consumers**

 
 
• These organisms, also called herbivores, feed directly on producers.
 
• Examples include cows, deer, and caterpillars.
 
 
 
• **Secondary Consumers**
 
 
• These are carnivores or omnivores that feed on primary consumers.
 
• Examples include frogs, small birds, and some fish.
 
 
 
• **Tertiary Consumers**
 
 
• These are apex predators that consume secondary consumers.
 
• Examples include lions, eagles, and sharks.

questions.question: In which of the following are CFCs NOT used?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Grinders__**.

**Note: **As per the official answer key, the correct answer is** Fire extinguishers** but in actual the correct answer would be** Grinders**. Traditionally, fire extinguishers have utilized halogens (CFCs), which today are well-known ozone-depleting agents. Grinders are tools used for grinding, cutting, and shaping materials, usually in industrial settings.

CFCs are not used in grinders

**Source:** https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/earth-and-planetary-sciences/fire-extinguisher#:~:text=Traditionally%2C%20fire%20extinguishers%20have%20utilized,systems%20and%20contaminate%20water%20supplies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**Fire Extinguishers:**

__
 
• Certain types of fire extinguishers, especially older models, used halons, which are chemically related to CFCs and also have ozone-depleting properties.

**Grinders:**

 
• Grinders are tools used for grinding, cutting, and shaping materials, usually in industrial settings.
 
• CFCs are not used in grinders because there is no need for refrigerants or propellants in these types of tools.

**Aerosol Sprays:**

 
• CFCs were commonly used as propellants in aerosol sprays such as deodorants, hair sprays, and sprays for various household products.
 
• Due to their harmful impact on the ozone layer, alternative propellants have been developed and are now used instead.

**Refrigerators:**

 
• CFCs were widely used as refrigerants in refrigeration systems, including refrigerators, freezers, and air conditioners.
 
• Due to the regulations concerning ozone depletion, CFCs have been replaced with more environmentally friendly refrigerants, but they historically were used in these applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ozone Layer Depletion**

 
 
• CFCs release chlorine atoms upon exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation, which then break down ozone molecules in the stratosphere.
 
• This process leads to the thinning of the ozone layer, which protects the Earth from harmful UV radiation.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol**
 
 
• An international treaty signed in 1987 aimed at phasing out the production and use of substances that deplete the ozone layer, including CFCs.
 
• The protocol has been successful in reducing the emissions of ozone-depleting substances.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Compounds**
 
 
• Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) and other environmentally friendly refrigerants have been developed as alternatives to CFCs.
 
• HFCs do not deplete the ozone layer but are potent greenhouse gases, necessitating further advancements in sustainable alternatives.

questions.question: Select the option that shows all biodegradable substances.

options.text: Bubble packs, Vegetable peelings, Stale bread
Glass bottle, Milk packets, Egg shells, Banana peel
Medicine bottle, Old shoe, Stale biscuits

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Biodegradable substances are those that can be broken down by natural processes involving microorganisms.
 
• Option 1 includes eggshells, tea leaves, and potato peelings, all of which are organic materials and can decompose naturally.
 
• Bubble packs (option 2) and glass bottles (option 3) are non-biodegradable as they do not decompose naturally.
 
• Medicine bottles and old shoes (option 4) are also non-biodegradable because they are made of synthetic materials that resist natural decomposition.
 
• Option 1 correctly identifies substances that are biodegradable and can return nutrients to the ecosystem through natural processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-biodegradable Substances**

 
 
• These are materials that cannot be broken down by natural processes. Examples include plastics, metals, and glass.
 
• Non-biodegradable substances can accumulate in the environment and cause pollution.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Biodegradable Materials**
 
 
• Using biodegradable materials helps reduce waste and environmental pollution.
 
• They contribute to sustainable practices by returning nutrients to the soil through decomposition.
 
 
 
• **Composting**
 
 
• Composting is a process that involves the decomposition of organic waste to produce compost, a nutrient-rich soil amendment.
 
• It is an effective way to manage biodegradable waste and improve soil health.

questions.question: What percentage of solar energy is captured by green plants in terrestrial ecosystem?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 percent**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Green plants in terrestrial ecosystems capture only about **1 percent** of the solar energy that reaches them.
 
• This energy is utilized for the process of **photosynthesis**, where it is converted into chemical energy.
 
• The chemical energy is stored in the form of **glucose** and other organic molecules.
 
• The efficiency of solar energy capture by plants is relatively low due to various factors such as **reflection, transmission, and absorption of light** by non-photosynthetic parts.
 
• Despite the low percentage, this energy forms the base of the **food chain** in terrestrial ecosystems, supporting a wide range of life forms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Photosynthesis**

 
 
• It is the process by which green plants, algae, and some bacteria convert light energy into chemical energy.
 
• Photosynthesis primarily occurs in the **chloroplasts** of plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transfer in Ecosystems**
 
 
• Energy captured by plants is transferred to herbivores when they consume plants, and subsequently to carnivores when they consume herbivores.
 
• Only about **10 percent** of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.
 
 
 
• **Solar Energy Utilization**
 
 
• A large portion of solar energy is not used for photosynthesis and is instead reflected or absorbed as heat.
 
• Plants have evolved various adaptations to maximize their **light absorption efficiency**.

questions.question: What happens when pea plants showing two different characteristics (the tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait), rather than just one are bred with each other?

options.text: The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.
They are all tall and have round seeds in F2 generation.
Some F1 progeny are tall plants with round seeds, and some are short plants with wrinkled seeds.
The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are dependently inherited.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tall/short trait and the round seed/wrinkled seed trait are independently inherited.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When pea plants showing two different characteristics are bred, each trait is inherited independently of the other.
 
• This observation is consistent with Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, which states that alleles of different genes assort independently of one another during gamete formation.
 
• The F1 progeny will all be heterozygous, exhibiting the dominant traits for both characteristics.
 
• In the F2 generation, a 9:3:3:1 phenotypic ratio is typically observed, showing independent assortment.
 
• This means that the combination of traits can vary, resulting in plants that may be tall with round seeds, tall with wrinkled seeds, short with round seeds, or short with wrinkled seeds.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Law of Segregation**

 
 
• Mendel's first law states that the two alleles for a heritable character segregate (separate) during gamete formation and end up in different gametes.
 
• This law ensures that offspring acquire one allele from each parent for each trait.
 
 
 
• **Law of Dominance**
 
 
• According to this law, in a heterozygote, one trait will conceal the presence of another trait for the same characteristic.
 
• The dominant allele is expressed in the phenotype, while the recessive allele is masked in the presence of the dominant allele.
 
 
 
• **Monohybrid Cross**
 
 
• A cross between individuals focusing on a single trait, which illustrates the inheritance of one characteristic.
 
• It typically results in a 3:1 phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation.

questions.question: Every trait in an organism is influenced by which of the following?

options.text: By both maternal and paternal DNA equally
More by paternal DNA than maternal DNA

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**By both maternal and paternal DNA equally**__.

**Note:** As per the official answer key, the correct answer is **Option 3** but in actual the correct answer would be** Option 2. **In sexually reproducing organisms, each trait is influenced by the DNA inherited from both parents. During fertilization, an organism receives half of its genetic material from its mother (maternal DNA) and the other half from its father (paternal DNA). Therefore, traits are influenced equally by both maternal and paternal DNA. This allows for a combination of genetic information that contributes to the unique characteristics of the offspring.

Source: https://web.iitd.ac.in/~sumeet/Genetics/CHAP%209.pdf

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Traits in an organism are influenced by **both maternal and paternal DNA equally**.
 
• Each parent contributes one set of chromosomes, thus providing half of the genetic material to the offspring.
 
• Genetic traits and characteristics are determined by the combination of genes inherited from both parents.
 
• During sexual reproduction, the offspring receive a mix of genetic material, which contributes to genetic diversity.
 
• Understanding the inheritance patterns helps in studying genetic diseases and traits that run in families.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mendelian Inheritance**

 
 
• Gregor Mendel's principles of inheritance describe how traits are passed from parents to offspring through dominant and recessive alleles.
 
• His experiments with pea plants laid the foundation for modern genetics.
 
 
 
• **Sex-linked Traits**
 
 
• These are traits associated with genes located on the sex chromosomes (X and Y).
 
• Examples include hemophilia and color blindness, which are often more common in males due to their single X chromosome.
 
 
 
• **Polygenic Inheritance**
 
 
• Some traits are controlled by multiple genes, resulting in a range of phenotypes.
 
• Examples include skin color, height, and weight, which are influenced by the interaction of several genes.

questions.question: Which of the following actions is responsible for the survival of species over time?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Variation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Variation is crucial for the survival of species as it provides a pool of different traits that can be beneficial in changing environments.
 
• Genetic variation increases the likelihood that some individuals in a population will possess traits suited to new or altered conditions.
 
• Natural selection acts on variations within a population, leading to the survival and reproduction of individuals with advantageous traits.
 
• Over time, these advantageous traits become more common in the population, aiding in the species' adaptation and survival.
 
• Without variation, a species may not be able to adapt to environmental changes, leading to extinction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Conservation**

 
 
• Conservation involves protecting and preserving natural resources and the environment.
 
• It helps in maintaining biodiversity and preventing the extinction of species.
 
 
 
• **Reproduction**
 
 
• Reproduction is the biological process by which new individual organisms are produced.
 
• It ensures the continuation of species but does not alone guarantee the survival of species over time.
 
 
 
• **Struggle for Existence**
 
 
• The struggle for existence refers to the competition between individuals of a species for limited resources.
 
• It is a driving force in natural selection, leading to the survival of the fittest.

questions.question: Citrus fruits, which are essential components of a kitchen, contain Vitamin C. Vitamin C is also known as _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ascorbic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Vitamin C, also known as ascorbic acid, is a water-soluble vitamin essential for various bodily functions.
 
• It is a potent antioxidant that helps protect cells from damage caused by free radicals.
 
• Ascorbic acid is crucial for the synthesis of collagen, which is vital for the health and repair of tissues, including skin, blood vessels, and bones.
 
• Vitamin C enhances the absorption of non-heme iron, which is the type of iron found in plant-based foods.
 
• A deficiency in Vitamin C can lead to scurvy, characterized by symptoms such as anemia, weakness, gum disease, and skin problems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sources of Vitamin C:**

 
 
• Citrus fruits like oranges, lemons, and grapefruits are rich sources of Vitamin C.
 
• Other sources include strawberries, kiwi, bell peppers, broccoli, and Brussels sprouts.
 
 
 
• **Role in Immune Function:**
 
 
• Vitamin C is known to boost the immune system by stimulating the production and function of white blood cells.
 
• It also strengthens the skin's defense system and helps wounds heal faster.
 
 
 
• **Daily Recommended Intake:**
 
 
• The recommended daily intake of Vitamin C varies by age, gender, and life stage.
 
• For adults, the recommended daily allowance is about 90 mg for men and 75 mg for women.
 
 
 
• **Vitamin C Supplements:**
 
 
• Vitamin C supplements are available in various forms, including tablets, capsules, and chewable gummies.
 
• It is generally considered safe, but excessive intake can lead to side effects such as stomach upset and diarrhea.

questions.question: Recombinant proteins, often seen in the news, are _____.

options.text: proteins synthesised by transgene in host cell by rDNA technology
proteins synthesised in mutated cell lines

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**proteins synthesised by transgene in host cell by rDNA technology**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Recombinant proteins** are synthesized using **recombinant DNA (rDNA) technology**, which involves inserting a transgene into a host cell.
 
• This process enables the **production of specific proteins** by leveraging the host organism’s cellular machinery.
 
• These proteins have a wide range of applications, including **therapeutics, diagnostics, and industrial enzymes**.
 
• Host cells used in this technology can vary and include **bacteria, yeast, insect, and mammalian cells**, depending on the requirements.
 
• Examples of recombinant proteins include **insulin, growth hormones, monoclonal antibodies, and vaccines**.
 
• The process involves **isolation of the gene of interest, insertion into a vector, transformation into a host cell, and expression of the protein**.
 
• Recombinant proteins are critical in the production of biosimilars and biopharmaceuticals for treating diseases like **diabetes, cancer, and autoimmune disorders**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Proteins synthesised in animal models**__

 __
 
• These proteins are naturally produced in **animal models** for research purposes, such as studying the effects of certain genes or drugs.
 
• They are not produced using **recombinant DNA technology** but are derived from the animal's native cellular processes.
 
 
 
• **Natural proteins found in bacteria**__
 __
 
• These are proteins that are **naturally synthesized by bacteria** as part of their metabolic processes.
 
• Examples include enzymes like **DNA polymerase** and proteins involved in bacterial growth and replication.
 
• These are not recombinant proteins as they are not produced through genetic modification.
 
 
 
• **Proteins synthesised in mutated cell lines**__
 
 
• These proteins are produced in **genetically altered cell lines** to study disease mechanisms or drug effects.
 
• However, this does not necessarily involve the use of **rDNA technology** and transgenes.

questions.question: Which type of RNA transports genetic information from the DNA in the nucleus to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm, where it directs protein synthesis?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**mRNA**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **mRNA** stands for **messenger RNA**.
 
• It is responsible for transporting **genetic information** from the **DNA** in the nucleus to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm, where **protein synthesis** occurs.
 
• During the process of **transcription**, DNA is used as a template to produce mRNA.
 
• The sequence of nucleotides in mRNA corresponds to the sequence of amino acids in a protein, following the rules of the **genetic code**.
 
• mRNA carries codons, which are specific sequences of three nucleotides that code for a particular **amino acid**.
 
• It plays a crucial role in the process of **translation**, where ribosomes decode the mRNA to synthesize proteins.
 
• mRNA has a short life span in the cell, as it is degraded after the protein synthesis process is complete.
 
• Its primary role is to act as an intermediary between the genetic material (DNA) and the machinery responsible for protein production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **tRNA**__

 __
 
• **tRNA** stands for **transfer RNA**.
 
• It plays a role in **translation** by bringing specific amino acids to the ribosome based on the codons in the mRNA.
 
• Each tRNA has an **anticodon** that pairs with a complementary codon on the mRNA.
 
 
 
• **snRNA**__
 __
 
• **snRNA** stands for **small nuclear RNA**.
 
• It is primarily involved in the process of **splicing** during the maturation of pre-mRNA in the nucleus.
 
• snRNAs are a component of **spliceosomes**, which remove introns from pre-mRNA.
 
 
 
• **rRNA**__
 
 
• **rRNA** stands for **ribosomal RNA**.
 
• It is a structural and functional component of **ribosomes**, which are the sites of protein synthesis.
 
• rRNA helps to catalyze the formation of **peptide bonds** between amino acids during translation.

questions.question: The combination of alleles at specific gene locations on an organism's chromosomes, representing its genetic constitution, is known as ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**genotype**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **genotype** refers to the genetic makeup of an organism. It is the combination of **alleles** at specific gene locations on the organism's chromosomes.
 
• It determines the hereditary characteristics of an organism and remains unchanged throughout its life.
 
• The genotype is represented by specific **letters** or symbols that indicate the alleles present, such as "AA," "Aa," or "aa."
 
• It is a crucial concept in **Mendelian genetics**, where traits are understood based on dominant and recessive alleles.
 
• The genotype interacts with the environment to produce the observable traits or physical expression, known as the **phenotype**.
 
• For example, in pea plants studied by **Gregor Mendel**, the genotype "TT" or "Tt" results in tall plants, whereas "tt" results in short plants.
 
• The study of genotypes is essential in understanding genetic disorders, inheritance patterns, and evolutionary biology.
 
• Modern technologies like **genotyping** and **DNA sequencing** help scientists analyze genotypes for medical and research purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DNA**__

 __
 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)** is the molecule that carries the genetic instructions for the development, functioning, growth, and reproduction of all known living organisms.
 
• It is composed of two strands forming a **double helix structure**, discovered by **James Watson and Francis Crick** in 1953.
 
• DNA contains the genetic information in sequences of **nucleotides**, which include adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G).
 
• While the genotype is the combination of alleles, DNA is the physical medium that stores and transmits genetic information.
 
 
 
• **Double Helix**__
 __
 
• The term **double helix** refers to the structure of DNA, consisting of two strands twisted around each other.
 
• It was first described by **Watson and Crick** based on the X-ray diffraction data produced by **Rosalind Franklin**.
 
• The strands are held together by **hydrogen bonds** between complementary bases (A pairs with T, C pairs with G).
 
• While the double helix is a structural property of DNA, the genotype is about the specific genetic information encoded within the DNA.
 
 
 
• **Phenotype**__
 
 
• The **phenotype** refers to the observable physical or biochemical characteristics of an organism, such as height, eye color, or enzyme activity.
 
• It is influenced by both the **genotype** and the environment.
 
• For example, two plants with the same genotype for height might vary in actual height due to differences in **soil quality**, **water availability**, or **sunlight exposure**.
 
• While the genotype is the genetic blueprint, the phenotype represents the expression of that blueprint.

questions.question: Which of the following physicists is renowned for their groundbreaking research on natural radioactivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Marie Curie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Marie Curie was a Polish-French physicist and chemist who is best known for her pioneering work on **radioactivity**.
 
• She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different scientific fields: **Physics (1903) and Chemistry (1911)**.
 
• Her groundbreaking research led to the discovery of the radioactive elements **polonium** and **radium**.
 
• Marie Curie coined the term **radioactivity** to describe the phenomenon of spontaneous emission of radiation by certain substances.
 
• Her work laid the foundation for advancements in nuclear physics, radiotherapy, and medical imaging technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Radioactivity:**

 
 
• It is a physical phenomenon where unstable atomic nuclei release energy in the form of radiation to achieve a stable state.
 
• There are three main types of radioactive emissions: **alpha particles, beta particles, and gamma rays**.
 
• Radioactivity is widely used in fields such as medicine, nuclear energy, and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Polonium and Radium:**
 
 
• Polonium was discovered by Marie Curie in 1898 and named after her homeland, Poland.
 
• Radium was discovered later in 1898 and is highly radioactive, used historically in cancer treatments.
 
 
 
• **Nobel Prizes:**
 
 
• Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel for their work on radioactivity.
 
• She won the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for her discovery of radium and polonium.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Marie Curie's Research:**
 
 
• Her findings led to the development of X-ray machines used in medical diagnostics.
 
• Her research contributed to the understanding of nuclear reactions and the development of nuclear energy.

questions.question: The process of converting sugar into alcohol by adding yeast is known as:

• The depletion of the ozone layer allows more **UV radiation** to reach the Earth's surface.
 
• Increased UV radiation can also harm **ecosystems**, affecting the growth and survival of plants and marine life.

• Ozone layer depletion is primarily associated with **increased UV radiation**, not directly with water pollution.
 
• However, UV radiation can affect aquatic ecosystems, indirectly impacting water quality.
 
 
 
• **Increases soil fertility**__
 
 
• Soil fertility is influenced by factors such as **nutrient content, organic matter, and microbial activity**.

• CFCs are known for their role in **ozone layer depletion** in the stratosphere.

• The **Montreal Protocol** was established in 1987 to phase out the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances, including CFCs.

questions.question: What are the units of inheritance, which Mendel referred to as 'factors,' now called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Genes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gregor Mendel, known as the father of genetics, referred to the units of inheritance as 'factors'. These are now known as **genes**.
 
• Genes are segments of DNA that carry hereditary information and are responsible for guiding the development, functioning, and reproduction of organisms.
 
• Each gene is located at a specific location on a chromosome and can exist in different forms known as alleles.
 
• Genes are the basic physical and functional units of heredity, made up of DNA, and determine specific traits by coding for proteins.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **DNA (Deoxyribonucleic Acid)**

 
 
• DNA is a molecule that carries genetic instructions used in the growth, development, functioning, and reproduction of all known living organisms and many viruses.
 
• The structure of DNA is a double helix, composed of two strands that coil around each other.
 
• Each strand of DNA is made up of nucleotides, which include a phosphate group, a sugar group, and a nitrogen base.
 
 
 
• **Chromosomes**
 
 
• Chromosomes are thread-like structures located within the nucleus of animal and plant cells.
 
• Each chromosome is made of protein and a single molecule of DNA, which contains many genes.
 
• Humans have 23 pairs of chromosomes, for a total of 46 chromosomes.
 
 
 
• **Alleles**
 
 
• Alleles are different versions of a gene that determine distinct traits that can be passed on from parents to offspring.
 
• An individual inherits two alleles for each gene, one from each parent.
 
• Alleles can be dominant or recessive, influencing the expression of traits.
 
 
 
• **Traits**
 
 
• Traits are characteristics or features that are influenced by genes and can be passed from one generation to another.
 
• Examples of traits include eye color, hair color, and height.
 
• Traits can be influenced by the environment as well as genetics.

questions.question: According to Mendel, which trait appeared in F1 progeny on crossing tall pea plants with short pea plants?

questions.question: Which of the following factors is primarily responsible for survival of species?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Variations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Variations are differences in traits among individuals of the same species, which can be inherited.
 
• They are essential for natural selection, as they provide the raw material for evolution.
 
• Variations allow some individuals to adapt better to their environment, increasing their chances of survival and reproduction.
 
• Over time, beneficial variations accumulate in the population, leading to evolutionary changes.
 
• Examples of variations include differences in coloration, size, shape, and resistance to diseases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural Selection**

 
 
• It is a process by which organisms better adapted to their environment tend to survive and produce more offspring.
 
• Charles Darwin popularized the concept of natural selection as the mechanism of evolution.
 
• Natural selection acts on variations within a population, favoring those traits that enhance survival and reproduction.
 
 
 
• **Mutation**
 
 
• Mutations are changes in the DNA sequence that can lead to new variations.
 
• They can be caused by errors during DNA replication, exposure to certain chemicals, or radiation.
 
• While many mutations are neutral or harmful, some can provide beneficial traits that enhance survival.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation**
 
 
• Adaptation refers to the process by which a species becomes better suited to its environment.
 
• It involves the accumulation of beneficial variations over time through natural selection.
 
• Adaptations can be structural, behavioral, or physiological.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Drift**
 
 
• Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequencies in a population, often having a larger effect in small populations.
 
• It can lead to the loss or fixation of alleles over time.
 
• Unlike natural selection, genetic drift does not necessarily favor traits that are beneficial for survival.

• Common agents of seed dispersal include wind, water, and animals.
 
• Sunlight does not play a direct role in the dispersal of seeds; it is critical for seed germination and plant growth.
 
• Wind dispersal is seen in plants like dandelions and maples, where seeds are light and can be carried by the wind.
 
• Water dispersal is common in aquatic plants and plants near water bodies, where seeds are buoyant and can float away.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Animal Dispersal:** Animals can disperse seeds by eating fruits and excreting the seeds or by carrying seeds on their fur.
 
• **Explosive Mechanism:** Some plants have evolved mechanisms to forcibly eject seeds, such as in the case of touch-me-not plants.
 
• **Gravity Dispersal:** Seeds can simply fall from the plant to the ground and roll away, a method known as barochory.
 
• **Seed Germination:** The process by which a seed develops into a new plant, requiring optimal conditions of moisture, temperature, and sunlight.
 
• **Ecological Importance:** Seed dispersal helps maintain plant diversity, colonize new habitats, and ensure survival of species in varying environments.

questions.question: In which process multicellular organisms break into smaller pieces upon maturation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fragmentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fragmentation is a form of asexual reproduction where an organism breaks into two or more fragments upon maturation.
 
• Each fragment develops into a new individual, identical to the parent organism.
 
• This process is common in certain multicellular organisms such as sponges, starfish, and some annelid worms.
 
• Fragmentation allows for rapid population increase, particularly in environments with abundant resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sporulation**

 
 
• Sporulation is a process in which an organism forms spores that can develop into new individuals.
 
• It is observed in fungi, algae, and some bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Regeneration**
 
 
• Regeneration involves the regrowth of a lost or damaged part of the organism.
 
• It can occur in both asexual reproduction and healing processes.
 
• Common examples include the regeneration of starfish arms and lizard tails.
 
 
 
• **Fission**
 
 
• Fission is a form of asexual reproduction where an organism divides into two or more parts, each becoming a new organism.
 
• This process is typical in prokaryotic organisms like bacteria.
 
 
 
• **Asexual Reproduction**
 
 
• Asexual reproduction involves the generation of offspring without the fusion of gametes.
 
• It results in genetically identical offspring, known as clones.
 
• Common methods include binary fission, budding, and vegetative propagation.
